items.title: Three bodies recovered from flood-hit Chilime hydropower project three weeks later
items.blurb: Rescuers found the bodies inside a tunnel after the August 26 floods, with the search for additional victims continuing.

items.title: Timure was a bustling border hub. In hours, the floods wiped it off the map
items.blurb: More than 250 houses and other structures were swept away in the border settlement, leaving just six damaged houses standing and hundreds of people unaccounted for.

items.title: Bouldin meets Shah, offers US support for Nepal’s disaster recovery
items.blurb: The US chargé d’affaires expressed condolences over the Rasuwa floods as the prime minister called for greater global cooperation on climate-related risks.

items.title: Wagle to hold three high-level policy dialogues during India visit
items.blurb: Finance minister will engage Indian diplomats, business leaders and development policymakers, with flood reconstruction, investment, trade and connectivity expected to feature in his meetings.

items.title: India renews Nepal’s power import permit but leaves export approvals pending
items.blurb: Three hydropower projects have lost their export permits as Nepal seeks to sell surplus monsoon electricity while relying on India for winter supplies.

items.title: Their loved ones are gone. The law says they are still missing
items.blurb: Families of those swept away by the August 26 flood are performing funeral rites without bodies. But they cannot secure death certificates or claim relief, compensation, insurance and other entitlements.

items.title: A single landslide has choked Kathmandu for weeks. Dependable backup routes must be built
items.blurb: The Prithvi Highway disruption underscores the need for dependable alternative routes.

items.title: How disasters create fertile ground for human trafficking
items.blurb: There is seemingly an almost curated web of favourable conditions laid out especially for traffickers.

items.title: Repeated Tatopani closures deepen uncertainty for traders
items.blurb: The latest shutdown has stranded more than 45 containers in China, while years of disruptions have caused heavy losses for traders and businesses.

items.title: More tigers, more conflict, but too little room for those rescued
items.blurb: Nepal’s tiger population has grown to 429, but its only zoo and rescue centres lack adequate space and facilities for tigers rescued from settlements or too old or injured to survive in the wild.

items.title: Pelega hill in Nawalparasi has been smoking for years. Now experts want answers
items.blurb: Local residents say smoke has emerged from different spots on the hill for decades, but has grown thicker in recent months.

items.title: Ten families at risk as landslide threatens Baitadi village
items.blurb: A landslide that destroyed one house has left the entire village vulnerable, prompting authorities to urge households to relocate to safer areas.

items.title: Footbridges rise again from flood wreckage
items.blurb: Repairs and reconstruction are underway on 53 footbridges damaged by the August 26 flood along the Trishuli corridor, restoring vital links to markets, schools, health services and jobs.

items.title: Weeks after the Nepal flood disaster, families of the missing hold out hope
items.blurb: With 5,130 people still missing in Nepal and hundreds unaccounted for in China, families are scouring hospitals, contacting authorities and tracking digital clues for any sign their loved ones survived.
